theorem Smooth.section_component_iff_of_isPullback {P T P' T' : Scheme.{u}} (g : P ⟶ T)
    [Smooth g] [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g] (σ : T ⟶ P) (hσ : σ ≫ g = 𝟙 T)
    (g' : P' ⟶ T') (σ' : T' ⟶ P') (a : P' ⟶ P) (b : T' ⟶ T)
    (sq : IsPullback a g' g b) (hσ' : σ' ≫ g' = 𝟙 T') (hsec : σ' ≫ a = b ≫ σ) :
    ∀ p' : P', (p' ∈ connectedComponentIn (g' ⁻¹' {g' p'}) (σ' (g' p'))) ↔
      a p' ∈ connectedComponentIn (g ⁻¹' {g (a p')}) (σ (g (a p')))

title: Component predicate preserved by local noetherian model
statement: Let g:P\to T be smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with section σ:T\to P. Let g':P'\to T', a:P'\to P and b:T'\to T form a cartesian square. Let σ':T'\to P' be a section of g' such that σ'≫a=b≫σ. For every p' in P', membership of p' in the connected component of σ'(g'(p')) in its g'-fibre is equivalent to membership of a(p') in the connected component of σ(g(a(p'))) in its g-fibre.

proof.text: At t=b(g'(p')), the section point belongs to the fibre by the section identity. Apply the generalized ambient-open helper to this fibre subspace. The helper applies Mathlib isOpen_connectedComponent and isOpen_induced_iff to any locally connected subspace of an arbitrary topological space; for an ambient point outside that subspace the component is empty and the empty open suffices. It has no scheme or finite-type hypothesis. The fibre is locally connected by the existing locally-finite-type fibre instances. Cut out the resulting component by U and restrict the cartesian square along U.

Lift the residue-field-valued section to U and its fibre. The component fibre is nonempty and preconnected, hence connected. Apply GeometricallyConnected.of_connectedSpace_of_section to this connected fibre and its rational point. Apply geometrically_connectedSpace along the fibre pullback square from isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback, and transfer through fiberHomeo. Its image in P' is preconnected and contains the distinguished section point and p', so p' lies in the component of the section.

Conversely, continuity of a maps the component in P' to a preconnected subset of the original fibre containing the original section point. Section compatibility identifies this point, and the cartesian-square equation identifies the fibre. Apply subset_connectedComponentIn to get the reverse implication.
